title: Healthz 503 and non-zero exit when upstream child dies
description:
Goal (decision: /healthz -> 503 AND process exits non-zero): when the child transport is closed, `/healthz` returns 503 and the proxy exits with status 1 so the orchestrator restarts it. Today the proxy keeps running and `/healthz` says `ok` after the child dies (verified). README and AGENTS.md also disagree on this.

Depends on: graceful-shutdown issue (reuse its CancellationToken shutdown path).

Files: src/http.rs (`router_with`, `router`, `serve_*`), src/main.rs, tests/proxy.rs, README.md, AGENTS.md.

Steps:
1. `tilth_deps src/http.rs` first (`router_with` is pub, used by tests).
2. Add `healthy: impl Fn() -> bool + Clone + Send + Sync + 'static` to `router_with`. `/healthz` returns `(StatusCode::OK, HEALTH_BODY)` if `healthy()`, else `(StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, "upstream unavailable")`.
3. In `router`: pass `move || !peer_for_health.is_transport_closed()` (`peer_for_health` = another Arc clone of `upstream.peer()`; `Peer::is_transport_closed` exists in rmcp 3.5.1).
4. Update `router_with` callers in http.rs tests to pass `|| true`.
5. In `serve_*`: spawn a watcher checking `is_transport_closed()` every 1s; when true -> `tracing::error!`, cancel the shutdown token, and make `serve` return `Err(anyhow!("upstream MCP server exited"))` so main exits 1. main.rs must still run upstream shutdown.
6. FIRST verify `is_transport_closed()` actually flips to true after `kill -9` of the child. If not: STOP and report.
7. Tests:
   - tests/proxy.rs `an_upstream_failure_does_not_leak_child_stderr`: after the failed call, GET /healthz -> 503.
   - http.rs unit: `router_with(cfg, stub, || false)` on /healthz -> 503.
8. Make README "Operational behavior" and AGENTS.md (`src/upstream.rs` line) both say: a dead child -> /healthz 503 and non-zero exit.

Commit: `fix(http): report and exit on an unavailable upstream`

title: Graceful shutdown with 3s deadline, close SSE on signal
description:
Goal (decision: 3s grace): after SIGTERM/SIGINT the process exits within SHUTDOWN_GRACE = 3s even with open SSE streams or stalled request bodies, and still reaps the child. Today plain HTTP has no drain deadline and TLS uses `graceful_shutdown(None)`; one idle SSE stream kept the process alive >3s after SIGTERM (verified), so main never reaches child cleanup. README claims ~1s.

File: src/http.rs (+ tests, README.md, AGENTS.md).

Steps:
1. `const SHUTDOWN_GRACE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(3);`
2. One `tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken` per `serve` call (tokio-util already a dep). Change `server_config(cfg)` -> `server_config(cfg, token.clone())` and set `config.cancellation_token = token;` (pub field on rmcp StreamableHttpServerConfig; ends rmcp SSE streams on cancel). Thread the token through `router`/`router_with` (`tilth_deps` first).
3. Spawn one task: `shutdown_signal().await; token.cancel();`
4. Plain HTTP: `.with_graceful_shutdown(token.clone().cancelled_owned())`, then:
   ```rust
   tokio::select! {
       r = server => r.context("HTTP server failed"),
       () = async { token.cancelled().await; tokio::time::sleep(SHUTDOWN_GRACE).await } => {
           tracing::warn!("shutdown grace expired; dropping open connections");
           Ok(())
       }
   }
   ```
5. TLS (manual + ACME): `graceful_shutdown(Some(SHUTDOWN_GRACE))`, triggered by the token.
6. Test (new tests/shutdown.rs or tests/tls.rs style; copy `spawn_once`/`free_port`/`fixture_binary`/`proxy_binary` patterns from tests/tls.rs which spawn the real binary): start without TLS, initialize a session, open `GET /mcp` with `Accept: text/event-stream` and keep it open, send `kill -TERM <pid>`; assert exit within SHUTDOWN_GRACE + 2s and the child pid is gone (`kill -0` fails).
7. README: "within a few seconds"; AGENTS.md: replace "~1s".

Commit: `fix(http): bound graceful shutdown and close SSE streams on signal`

title: Proxy: forward client _meta, strip spoofed caller
description:
Goal (decision: forward client _meta, always strip caller key): custom client `_meta` reaches the child, and a client can NEVER set `io.stdio2http/caller` itself (any auth mode). Today client `_meta` is silently dropped (verified: `{"custom":"keep-me"}` never arrives).

Background: rmcp moves wire `_meta` into `RequestContext.meta` (pub field, type `RequestMetaObject`); typed `params.meta` is always empty server-side.

Depends on: list-requests caller-stamping issue (same helpers).

File: src/proxy.rs (+ tests/proxy.rs, README.md).

Steps:
1. Pure helper `fn merged_meta(client: &RequestMetaObject, subject: Option<&str>) -> Option<RequestMetaObject>`:
   - clone `client`; ALWAYS remove `CALLER_META_KEY`; remove `progressToken` (rmcp sets its own);
   - if subject is Some insert it under `CALLER_META_KEY`;
   - return None if empty.
2. Every handler sets the params meta from `merged_meta(&context.meta, caller.as_deref())`. For paginated `Option` requests only create `Some(params)` when merged_meta returns Some.
3. Unit tests: custom key kept; spoofed caller removed when subject None; replaced when Some; empty + no subject -> None.
4. E2E in tests/proxy.rs (auth none): raw HTTP `tools/call whoami` with `params._meta["io.stdio2http/caller"]="mallory"` -> result `"<none>"`.
5. README: client `_meta` is forwarded; the caller key is always set by the proxy only.

Commit: `fix(proxy): forward client _meta and strip spoofed caller identity`

title: HTTP: bind MCP sessions to the authenticating key
description:
Goal: in bearer / identity-forward mode, a request carrying `Mcp-Session-Id` gets `404 Not Found: Session not found` unless it uses the SAME key that created that session (POST, GET resume, DELETE). Verified today: Bob's key can DELETE Alice's session (202, then Alice gets 404). Session IDs are UUIDs, so an ID must leak first. HIGH complexity — follow the steps exactly.

Depends on: config-validation issue.

Files: src/auth.rs, src/http.rs, new src/session_owner.rs (`pub mod session_owner;` in lib.rs), tests/proxy.rs, README.md.

Steps:
1. Principal: in auth.rs add `#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)] pub struct Principal(usize);` = index of the matched key in `AuthState.keys` (never a secret). Make `authenticate` also return the index (e.g. `Allowed { subject, key_index: Option<usize> }`). In `authorize` insert `Principal(i)` into request extensions in BOTH bearer and identity-forward. Update existing auth tests.
2. session_owner.rs: `pub struct SessionOwners(Arc<std::sync::Mutex<HashMap<String, Principal>>>)` with `claim(id, p)`, `check(id, p) -> bool` (true if unknown or owned by p), `release(id)`. Never hold the mutex across `.await`.
3. Middleware `enforce(State(owners), req, next)` placed INSIDE the auth layer (Principal already set):
   - no Principal (auth none) -> `next.run(req)` unchanged
   - header `Mcp-Session-Id` present and `!owners.check(id, p)` -> 404, body `Not Found: Session not found` (identical to rmcp)
   - remember method + id; `let resp = next.run(req).await;`
   - response has `Mcp-Session-Id` and request had none -> `owners.claim(new_id, p)`
   - (DELETE and 2xx) or response 404 -> `owners.release(id)`
4. Wiring in `router_with`: add `.layer(from_fn_with_state(owners, enforce))` BEFORE the auth `.layer(...)` (axum: earlier layer = inner). Add a test proving the order.
5. E2E tests in tests/proxy.rs with raw reqwest (like `assert_401`):
   - `another_key_cannot_delete_a_session` (Bob DELETE -> 404; Alice tools/list -> 200)
   - `another_key_cannot_resume_a_session` (Bob GET + `Last-Event-ID: 0/0` -> 404)
   - `another_key_cannot_post_to_a_session` (Bob POST tools/list -> 404)
   - `owner_can_delete_own_session` (Alice DELETE -> 202, next -> 404)
   - existing auth-none tests still pass
6. Code comment (one line): entries for sessions expired by rmcp (300s idle) are removed only when that id is used again.
7. README Limitations: sessions are bound to the authenticating key; upstream child state is still shared.

Commit: `fix(http): bind MCP sessions to the authenticating key`

title: HTTP: CORS preflight for configured origins
description:
Goal (decision: support browsers when --allowed-origin is set): browser CORS preflight from a configured origin succeeds without credentials. Today OPTIONS goes through auth -> 401 (verified), and rmcp returns 405 for OPTIONS anyway; there is no CORS response layer. AGENTS.md claims preflight stays open.

Depends on: session-binding issue (layer ordering in router_with).

Files: Cargo.toml, src/http.rs, src/config.rs, AGENTS.md.

Steps:
1. Add `tower-http = { version = "0.6", features = ["cors"] }` (already in lockfile via rmcp; check `cargo tree -i tower-http`).
2. In `router_with`, ONLY when `!cfg.allowed_origins.is_empty()`, add a `CorsLayer` as the OUTERMOST layer on the `/mcp` route (added after auth, so it wraps auth):
   - allow_origin: exact values from `cfg.allowed_origins` (parse to `HeaderValue`; reject invalid values in `Config::validate`)
   - allow_methods: GET, POST, DELETE
   - allow_headers: authorization, content-type, x-api-key, mcp-session-id, mcp-protocol-version, last-event-id
   - expose_headers: mcp-session-id
   - NO allow_credentials; NEVER `Any`.
3. Tests (stub service in http.rs):
   - preflight from allowed origin -> 2xx + `access-control-allow-origin` = that origin, no key needed
   - preflight from another origin -> no ACAO header
   - no --allowed-origin -> unchanged (OPTIONS hits auth -> 401 in bearer)
   - non-OPTIONS still need a key
4. AGENTS.md `src/auth.rs` line: preflight is answered by the CORS layer only for configured origins.

Commit: `feat(http): answer CORS preflight for configured origins`

Problem: rmcp `LocalSessionManager` has no limit on concurrent sessions. Each `initialize` allocates a session, worker task and channels; idle sessions expire only after 300s. With default `--auth-mode none`, anyone reaching the port can flood sessions; with bearer, any valid key can.

Also covers: stale entries in the session-owner map (from the session-binding issue) for sessions rmcp expired without the id being reused.

Next step when picked up: check whether a newer rmcp exposes a session cap / expiry callback; otherwise design a cap with explicit 503 that tracks rmcp expiry. Do not implement without a design review.

description:
Goal: in identity-forward mode EVERY forwarded request carries `_meta["io.stdio2http/caller"]`. Today `tools/list` / `resources/list` / `resources/templates/list` / `prompts/list` sent WITHOUT `params` reach the child with no identity (verified at runtime).

File: src/proxy.rs.

Steps:

   fn insert_subject<T: rmcp::model::RequestParamsMeta>(params: &mut T, subject: Option<String>)

   - `paginated_existing_cursor_is_kept`

description:
Goal: ACME renewal is scheduled from the issued certificate's real `notAfter`, not an assumed 90 days (a shorter-lived cert would renew after it expired; the wrong value is also persisted).

   - parse the first PEM block (`x509_parser::pem::parse_x509_pem`, then `.parse_x509()`)

title: stdio2http: MCP stdio -> Streamable HTTP proxy
description:
Plan file: ~/.opencode/plan/stdio2http-mcp-proxy.md

A small Rust binary that spawns one stdio MCP server as a child process and
re-exposes it over MCP Streamable HTTP (POST/GET/DELETE /mcp), so HTTP clients
on the container network can use a stdio-only server.

DESIGN
Two rmcp roles talking to each other, not a hand-rolled JSON-RPC pipe:

  HTTP client --StreamableHttpService--> ProxyHandler (ServerHandler)
                                                 |
                                                 | rmcp client Peer (Arc, shared)
                                                 v
                                        stdio MCP child (TokioChildProcess)

Upstream: TokioChildProcess::new(Command::new(prog).configure(..)) then
().serve(child) -> RunningService<RoleClient, ()> -> .peer(). One long-lived
child, connected once at startup.

Downstream: StreamableHttpService::new(factory, session_manager, config)
mounted on axum at /mcp. rmcp owns session ids, Mcp-Session-Id, SSE framing,
Last-Event-ID, content negotiation, and protocol negotiation.

ProxyHandler holds Arc<Peer<RoleClient, ()>>. Every ServerHandler method
forwards to that peer. The factory clones the Arc, so every HTTP session shares
the same child -- this is what "one long-lived process" means and why
concurrency is safe (rmcp multiplexes by JSON-RPC request id).

ASSUMPTIONS (flagged, not hidden)
1. Caller identity vs. one shared child: env vars are fixed at spawn and cannot
   vary per request. Resolved by forwarding identity PER REQUEST as namespaced
   _meta on forwarded JSON-RPC params. If the upstream instead needs a separate
   PROCESS per identity, that is a different design (process-per-session) and is
   NOT covered here. Confirm before the auth-mode-3 issue if that is the case.
2. No TLS in the proxy. Run behind a terminating proxy or on a trusted network.
3. Upstream server is stateless across sessions; if it keeps per-connection
   state, all HTTP callers share it. Single-tenant container, acceptable.
4. A dead child is fatal, not restarted: exit non-zero, let the orchestrator
   restart. Backoff restart is a v2 option.
5. rmcp pinned to 3.5.1 (spec 2026-07-28) at time of writing.

OUT OF SCOPE v1
Legacy SSE transport, multiple aggregated upstreams, per-session child
processes, auto-restart of a dead child, Tasks/MRTR passthrough.

KNOWN GAP
Notifications and server->client requests do NOT forward through a
ServerHandler that only proxies request/response. progress, tools/list_changed,
logging, sampling, and roots originate at the child with no path to the HTTP
client. Long-running tools appear to hang without progress; a tool calling
sampling fails. This is the main behavioral difference from supergateway, which
bridges these explicitly. Documented as unsupported in the v1 README.
close_reason: All 10 steps complete: 65 tests green, clippy -D warnings clean, SIGTERM reaps child

Arc<Peer<RoleClient, ()>>.

Methods to implement (thin pass-through plus error mapping):
  get_info, list_tools, call_tool, list_resources, read_resource,
  list_resource_templates, list_prompts, get_prompt, complete,
  subscribe, unsubscribe, set_level

Rules
- Map RmcpError / transport failure to ErrorData::internal_error.
- Never leak the child's stderr or the proxy's env into an error message
  returned to the client.
- Forward pagination params (Option<PaginatedRequestParams> / cursors)
  unchanged; do not re-implement cursors.

title: http.rs: axum router, /mcp, graceful shutdown
description:
Step 5 of the stdio2http plan.

Router::new()
  .route("/healthz", get(|| "ok"))
  .route_service("/mcp", StreamableHttpService::new(...))

StreamableHttpServerConfig::default() plus with_allowed_hosts(..) and
with_allowed_origins(..) from config. Only call disable_allowed_hosts() if
explicitly configured -- rmcp defaults allowed_hosts to loopback only, to
prevent DNS rebinding against locally running servers, so a public deployment
MUST set it.

Serve with axum::serve + with_graceful_shutdown on SIGTERM/SIGINT, then
peer.cancel() and child graceful_shutdown().

title: auth.rs: one tower layer, three modes
description:
Step 6 of the stdio2http plan.

A single tower layer over /mcp implementing all three access modes.

none
  pass through.

bearer
  Require Authorization: Bearer <key> or X-API-Key: <key> matching any
  configured key; else 401 with WWW-Authenticate. Constant-time comparison.
  Never log the presented or configured key.

identity-forward
  Verify as in bearer, derive a subject (the key itself, or a configured
  key=subject map), stash it in request extensions. Step 7 attaches it to
  forwarded params as _meta["io.stdio2http/caller"].

/healthz and CORS preflight stay open in all modes.

SECURITY
Constant-time compare only. No key in any log line at any level.

VERIFY
- table test: no header -> 401 in both modes; wrong key -> 401; correct key
  -> passes
- no key appears in captured log output
close_reason: auth.rs: 3 modes, constant-time compare, no key in logs (24 tests)

title: Wire caller identity into forwarded _meta
description:
Step 7 of the stdio2http plan.

In proxy.rs, read the caller subject out of
RequestContext<RoleServer>.extensions and merge it into the outgoing params'
meta map before forwarding.

rmcp injects the HTTP http::request::Parts into Extensions on the service
side, reachable from RequestContext -- see the StreamableHttpService docs
("Accessing HTTP request data from tool handlers").

WHY THIS IS THE ONLY CHANNEL
One long-lived child means env vars are fixed at spawn. Per-request _meta is
the only way to carry caller identity into a shared child. See Assumption 1 in
the epic: if the upstream needs a separate PROCESS per identity, this design
does not apply.

VERIFY
- integration test with two different keys asserts the stub server observed a
  different io.stdio2http/caller for each
close_reason: identity forwarded as _meta io.stdio2http/caller; distinct-caller integration test green
